resources.string: Optional, off by default. Camera data is a small file from the map data release; traffic is downloaded only when you turn it on. Your position is never sent.
Fixed cameras and average-speed sections, on the map and as an alert ahead.
Roads where the DGT says mobile radars may operate. Shown as stretches of road, never as points.
Accidents, closures, slow traffic, obstacles and bad weather (DGT, live).
Stopped vehicles with a connected V16 beacon (DGT, live).
There can be hundreds at any time.
For cameras with a known limit, stay quiet while you are under it. Cameras with an unknown limit always warn.

Mobile-radar zones are the stretches the DGT publishes; the exact spot of a mobile control is never shown. Alerts are informational and can be wrong or out of date. You are responsible for how you drive.

This turns on speed camera warnings.

- Sources: DGT (CC BY) and OpenStreetMap (ODbL). A camera on the list may not be switched on.
- Mobile-radar zones are road stretches published by the DGT. No live data, police controls or user reports.
- The file comes from the map data server you chose; nothing about your position is sent.
- Informational only: it may be wrong or out of date.

This downloads the DGT national traffic file (about 200 KB) from nap.dgt.es when you turn it on, press Update now or open the app with old data. It is filtered on your phone: your position and route are never sent. Offline mode blocks it.
Offline mode is on: nothing is downloaded until you turn it off.
Camera data: %1$d fixed cameras, %2$d average-speed sections, %3$d mobile-radar zones (%4$d drawable). File from %5$s.

the map catalog has no camera file; open Maps and refresh it
Mobile radars may operate on this stretch
Published by the DGT as a stretch of road, not as a position. A device may or may not be there, and the drawn line is approximate.
The source says where a camera may be, not that it is switched on.

Traffic data downloaded %1$s. It may have changed since.
